rationale:
Derivation from contract.md section C2 only (no implementation, oracle or sibling case was read).

(1) MOUNT RESOLUTION. Contract lines 95-99: 'parse mountinfo per proc.rst 3.5 (fields 1-6, optional fields until -, then fstype, source, super options) ... Candidate mounts: mount point equals realpath, or is /, or realpath starts with mount point + /.' The fixture's mountinfo text is written in the field layout of S082 (Linux procfs documentation at v7.2, Documentation/filesystems/proc.rst, section 3.5, lines 1965-1990; field table 1973-1983 with major:minor at 1975, separator at 1980, filesystem type at 1981, mount source at 1982, super options at 1983; example line 1970 '36 35 98:0 /mnt1 /mnt2 rw,noatime master:1 - ext3 /dev/root rw,errors=continue'). Each fixture line carries exactly fields 1-6, optional tagged fields (shared:N), the '-' separator, then fstype, source and super options, so every line parses. Field 5 (mount point) values present are /proc, /dev, /sys, /tmp, /srv/quota and /home. There is NO line whose field 5 is '/', so the root-mount candidate does not exist in this fixture.

(2) NO CANDIDATE FOR THE PATH. realpath is /srv/quota-probe/data. It equals no mount point. No mount point is '/'. The only mount point that is a lexical prefix of the realpath is /srv/quota, but the contract requires realpath to start with mount point + '/', i.e. '/srv/quota/', which is not a prefix of '/srv/quota-probe/data'; /proc/, /dev/, /sys/, /tmp/ and /home/ are likewise not prefixes. No candidate mount exists.

(3) VERDICT FOR THE PATH. Contract lines 99-100: 'None -> unknown basis no_covering_mount'. Contract lines 126-127: 'fstype/mount_point null when no covering mount'. Hence fstype=null, mount_point=null, quota_state=unknown, basis=no_covering_mount.

(4) ENFORCEMENT. The contract table (lines 108-122) has no row for the no-cover branch, but every row whose quota_state is 'unknown' carries enforcement 'n/a' (xfs conflicting options, xfs options absent, btrfs device unmapped, ext superblock unobservable, unsupported fstype). 'n/a' is therefore derived for quota_state=unknown here by that uniform table convention (ambiguity A-2 reported to L1).

(5) RUN VERDICT. Contract lines 132-135: setup error -> 2 QUOTA_SETUP; else any enabled -> 1 QUOTA_ENABLED; else any unknown -> 2 QUOTA_STATE_UNKNOWN; else 0 QUOTA_DISABLED. The fixture is well formed, so contract lines 92-93 do not trigger: it has exactly the five top-level keys (schema, mountinfo, paths, device_links, btrfs_sysfs), the path is absolute, and st_dev '259:2' is a well-formed major:minor. No path is enabled and the single path is unknown, so exit=2 and finding_id=QUOTA_STATE_UNKNOWN (not QUOTA_SETUP, which shares exit 2 but is a different finding_id).

(6) DISCRIMINATING POWER. st_dev '259:2' equals the major:minor of the non-covering '/srv/quota' mount. An implementation that accepts a bare lexical prefix (realpath.startswith(mount_point) without the contract's trailing '/') would select that xfs mount, classify it disabled with basis xfs_noquota_option and exit 0 QUOTA_DISABLED - an observably different answer, so this case fails such an implementation. An implementation that reads field 4 (root) as the mount point would also see '/' on several lines and resolve a mount, failing likewise.

(7) NOT ASSERTED. device_check, quota_option_keys and btrfs_qgroups_mode are not part of the compared path tuple (contract lines 144-145 compare path, fstype, mount_point, quota_state, enforcement, basis only), and with no covering mount the contract's device comparison (lines 100-103) is never reached, so no value is asserted for them.
